flip_era.detail: Care/cage ratio bottomed at 0.095 in FY2006 (immediate post-Katrina trough, all care lines slashed while police/sheriff held) and then MORE THAN DOUBLED to 0.31 by FY2011 adopted budget — the Katrina-rebuild itself. Ratio then PLATEAUED (0.31 FY2017, 0.32 FY2019, 0.37 FY2022): the flip is a one-time structural reset that completed by ~FY2011-2013, not an ongoing drift. The 2006 trough is itself the sharpest single-year care-ratio break in the series (-27% vs FY2005, care cut harder than cage) — a catastrophe-printed anti-care break that the recovery then reversed, overshooting to ~2x the pre-storm ratio by 2011 (driven by Library Fund doubling, Parks & Parkways recovery, and post-2005 dedicated NORD/parkway millages visible in the FY2020 book).

ratio_series.basis: press-labeled, INCOMPLETE care lane — not comparable

ledger_class.classification: city-operates-police, sheriff-operates-jail (hybrid cage ledger; unique among Band-A cities)
details: NOPD is fully city-run (like most cities, unlike STL where PD sits in a separate agency) — NOPD is the largest single cage line in every year of the series.

The Orleans jail (Orleans Justice Center / formerly Orleans Parish Prison) is run by the ORLEANS PARISH SHERIFF; the city pays a per-diem appropriation published as the 'Criminal Sheriff' line every year: 2004 actual $35.1M -> 2011 adopted $22.6M -> 2017 adopted $44.7M -> 2019 adopted $53.2M -> 2022 adopted $55.7M. This is city MONEY but not city OPERATIONS — it behaves like Memphis's state-cage external-money class on the money axis while sitting inside the city GF ledger.
Courts (Criminal District, Municipal+Traffic, Juvenile, Clerk, DA) are partial-external constitutional offices inside the GF — included in cage per spec.

Care lane is structurally city-heavy on operations but partly millage-dedicated (Library Fund 4.91 mills, NORD/Parkway dedicated mills 2.79 combined in FY2020 book) — care money is OWN-Raised, not external; the FEDERAL external-money class shows up in the FEMA Fund and CDBG (HUD) lanes funding capital recovery (libraries/parks rebuilt post-Katrina — e.g., FY2020 book lists a standing FEMA Fund as one of five major funds; the whole $2.1B FY2025-adopted capital book is FEMA/recovery-capital shaped).

Internal-money-class evidence: dedicated public-safety millages (6.40 police/fire double-triple platoon + 5.26 police + 7.71 fire in FY2020 book) means cage is ALSO partly tax-dedicated, muting discretionary-flip readings — both lanes carry dedicated mills, care via Library/NORD/Parkway, cage via police/fire platoon mills.

falsifier.claim: Katrina reset printed a real, durable care-ratio break (care/cage flipped from ~0.16 pre-storm to ~0.31-0.37 across the whole 2011-2022 run)
falsified_if: The 2004-2009 GF-basis columns are not comparable to the 2011+ all-funds columns — i.e., the apparent flip is a ledger-basis artifact. TEST: recompute FY2011 care/cage using GF-only columns (pdf-46 GF side only) vs pre-storm GF-only. GF-only FY2011 care = Recreation 8,002,700 + Parks 6,867,566 + Library 180,603 + Health 12,549,028 + HumSvc 2,727,542 = $30.3M vs pre-2004 care $27.5M — ratio barely moves pre-storm, so basis-flip alone CANNOT explain 0.31 vs 0.16: the flip survives the ledger-basis check (all-funds adds Library Fund $8.4M + Health $9.2M + HumSvc $1.3M = the difference; both add to CARE, not cage, so the flip is not an artifact).

Library Fund and NORD/Parkway dedicated mills were created/raised only in response to Katrina — i.e., the flip is a millage-referendum artifact rather than an appropriation flip. The care gain in 2011+ is ~half dedicated-millage (Library 4.91 mills) — a REAL but vote-printed structural change, not an appropriation-line flip.

Population denominator: pre-storm 485k vs post ~230k-385k — cage per-capita falls faster than care per-capita post-storm; the RATIO break could be a shrinkage artifact rather than a policy flip. Pre/post population-halving inflates both lanes per-capita, especially cage NOPD ($109M GF for ~230k = $475/head vs 2004 $252/head) — the ratio break to 0.31 by 2011 is therefore the WEAK direction for a true care-priority flip and the per-capita read should be run before claiming a flip.
